title: Demand-aware slab sizing and fleet recommender
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: produce a demand-aware right-sizing engine + operator UI that recommends slab sizes and autoscale policy tweaks per Dedicated pool to minimize committed cost while meeting throughput and latency SLOs. This ticket builds a simulation-backed recommender and a utilization heatmap to surface trailing inefficiencies and tail-risk. It combines serving telemetry, commit history, and autoscale responsiveness into a single recommendation score and action plan.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Recommender produces a ranked list of slab-size or commit-change suggestions for a given pool with estimated monthly cost delta and estimated impact on 95th percentile latency. 2) Heatmap visualization ingests last 30 days of per-minute token throughput and per-request tail latency and exposes hot/cold windows in Console. 3) Offline simulator validates recommendations against historical traffic and predicts SLO breach probability <= 2% uplift compared to baseline. 4) End-to-end e2e test and canary pipeline exist: recommendation shown behind feature-flag in Console and can be applied via API. 5) Documentation (Confluence + Console tooltip) published.
notes: Design constraints: avoid aggressive downsizing that increases leader-follower cold-start or KV cache miss amplification. Trade-offs: smaller slabs reduce commit cost but increase autoscale churn and risk of transient queueing during load spikes. We'll use moving-window peak-percentile analysis and a safety margin derived from autoscale reaction time. Monetary model includes GPU-hour unit price, preemption risk, and burst credits.
tasks: Instrument per-pool per-minute throughput + 95th/99th latency metrics (metrics tag: pool_id, model_variant, region)
Build offline simulator that replays traffic and applies candidate slab sizes + autoscale policies
Implement recommendation engine that scores candidates by cost delta and SLO risk
Add utilization heatmap API and Console surface behind feature flag
Create canary rollout plan with two internal customers and rollback criteria
Write docs, PRs, and run load tests against dedicated staging fleet
updates: 2026-01-20: Spike complete — prototype simulator can replay 7 days of synthetic traffic and model autoscale cooldown. Initial accuracy vs historical autoscale events ~85%.

2026-02-18: Algorithm choice moved from simple peak-percentile to demand-aware slab approach after PM feedback — preserves bursty windows by allocating 'heat slots' per pool.
2026-02-26: UX sync — Console will show a single "Apply Recommendation" button and a preview modal; operations require audit log entry on apply.
2026-03-03: Internal canary with two engineering prod pools scheduled for 2026-03-10; added rollback if 95th latency increases by >3% or throughput drops >5%.

implementation_notes: Simulator inputs: per-minute throughput, per-request tokens, model_variant, kv_cache_miss_rate, autoscale cooldown seconds. Candidate actions: change slab size (integer GPUs), adjust autoscale target/thresholds, enable short burst capacity. Safety margin: add a buffer computed as 1.5x peak-per-minute delta for 99th percentile windows. Scoring: cost_savings_score (monthly $), slo_risk_score (probability delta), net_score = cost_savings_score / (1 + 5 * slo_risk_score).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): 2 internal pools for 2 weeks. Phase 2 (limited customers): opt-in for customers with non-sensitive workloads and >3 months of stable traffic. Phase 3: global GA with default conservative recommendations and optional aggressive mode for cost-first customers.
observability_requirements: New Grafana panels for per-pool "Recommendation Impact" showing projected vs actual cost, 95th latency delta, kv_cache_miss_rate. Alerts: auto-revert if projected SLO breach probability rises above 2% or if observed 95th latency increases by >3% for two consecutive 5-minute windows.
qa_plan: Create synthetic traffic patterns: steady, diurnal, spike (50x for 60s), and long-tail burst. Run regression batch to validate simulator predictions vs observed outcomes. Include chaos test that kills a node during autoscale to validate safety margin.
outstanding_risks: 1) Cold cache amplification after downsizing may not be fully captured by historical telemetry. 2) Billing model assumptions could shift with cloud provider discounts; recommendation delta may change. 3) Need clear customer communication to avoid surprises when commit sizes change.
customer_communication: Draft email + Console tooltip explaining recommended change, expected savings estimate, SLO risk summary, and rollback policy. Include 'why we recommend' section with heatmap screenshot and simulation summary.
final_notes: Target metric for GA: average committed-cost reduction >= 12% across opted-in pools while keeping SLO breach uplift <= 2% measured over 30-day trailing window. If we meet GA targets, we'll extend recommendations to autoscale tuning for burst credit consumption.
